name: Pueblo of Santo Domingo grant, confirmed by Congress December 22, 1858 (Royce Area 669)
citation: Act of December 22, 1858, ch. 5, 11 Stat. 374 (confirmation); Act of June 7, 1924, 43 Stat. 636; Act of May 31, 1933, 48 Stat. 108
promises: Congress confirmed the Pueblo of Santo Domingo's land claim, as reported favorably by the Surveyor General of New Mexico, and ordered it surveyed and patented (Act of December 22, 1858, 11 Stat. 374).
The Act says the confirmation is only a relinquishment of the United States' own title and claim, and does not affect any adverse valid rights.
Royce records the grant as 74,743.11 acres, a Spanish grant of 1689 patented on November 1, 1864.

The Pueblo Lands Act of 1924 made the United States liable, and directed the Pueblo Lands Board to award compensation, for Pueblo land and water lost through the United States' failure to seasonably prosecute the Pueblo's rights (Section 6).
compensation: Section 2 of the Act of May 31, 1933 (48 Stat. 108) authorized $4,256.56 for the Pueblo of Santo Domingo "in addition to the awards made by the Pueblo Lands Board", in payment "in part" of the United States' liability declared by the 1924 Act, for replacement land and water or permanent improvements, in three annual instalments from fiscal year 1937. Section 3 separately authorized $66 for non-Indian claimants within the Pueblo of Santo Domingo whose claims the Board did not sustain. The Board's own award to the Pueblo was not read. The Act does not say which land the sum concerns.

openQuestions: The date 1886-10-01 in treaties.json is not an event date for this land. Royce prints the Pueblo grants under a block headed 'Oct. 1, Act of Congress, Stat. L. XI, 374'; 11 Stat. 374 is the Act of December 22, 1858, which confirmed the grant. This is land the Pueblo kept, not land it ceded. Not edited.
Whether the Pueblo of Santo Domingo elected under Section 6 of the 1933 Act to accept the sum in full discharge, and when it was actually appropriated and paid, was not researched.
Kewa Pueblo's own account was not located (kewa-nsn.us returned 403).
The statute link in treaties.json (ops.libs.uga.edu) was not used; the Act was read on govinfo.

How the 1927 Board finding on the 17,655-acre overlap with La Majada and Mesita de Juana Lopez was finally resolved after the 1976 denial of summary judgment (Docket 355, later in the Court of Claims) is a lead for a deeper pass; it would be a grant-specific finding.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): status lowered from broken to no-breach-found. Both breaches rested only on the 1933 Act, which names the Pueblo but not the grant or any tract. Section 6 of the 1924 Act limits compensation to land inside a granted or confirmed tract, but no source opened in this pass says the divested land lay inside this grant (Royce's area), or that this was the Pueblo's only granted or confirmed tract in 1924. Lead: the Pueblo Lands Board's report on this Pueblo (Senate Committee on Indian Affairs, Survey of Conditions of the Indians, part 20, 1932, pp. 10705-11317; HathiTrust blocked robots) or a Tenth Circuit review of its award, like 47 F.2d 446 for San Juan.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): the Act of May 31, 1933 (48 Stat. 108, read on govinfo) has no findings or preamble. Its title calls it a payment "in part" of the liability declared by the 1924 Act; section 2 adds sums "in addition to the awards made by the Pueblo Lands Board" and names pueblos, not grants or tracts. It is not, on its face, an admission that the Board's compensation was inadequate, and the Indian Claims Commission later held that Congress, acting as trustee, paid full market value for the lost land and that there was no Fifth Amendment taking (39 Ind. Cl. Comm. 34, 1976; 33 Ind. Cl. Comm. 82, 1974, for Taos land outside the town). The 1977 Commission remark that Congress "determined the Board was unfair" (41 Ind. Cl. Comm. 29) is a general description in Santa Clara's case, not a finding about this Pueblo. The 1933 Act is therefore not counted as a breach.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Pueblo, Santo Domingo, Santo Domingo grant; Pueblo of Santo Domingo v. United States, 227 Ct. Cl. 265 (April 22, 1981) refused to let the Pueblo withdraw from its 1969 stipulation that its aboriginal lands outside the grant were taken, and does not reach the La Majada overlap; the ICC aboriginal-title decisions found expressly exclude the confirmed grants (e.g. 30 Ind. Cl. Comm. 234, 1973), so nothing new inside this grant.
today: The grant remains the Pueblo's land base. Land and water that passed to non-Indians under the 1924 Act was compensated, not returned; where it lay is not established here. In its Pueblo Lands Act claim (Indian Claims Commission Docket 355, heard with three other pueblos) the Commission held on February 10, 1971 that neither the Act nor the Board's actions were a Fifth Amendment taking, and on September 16, 1976 that Congress, acting as trustee, had paid full market value for the lost land, so no interest was due. On December 22, 1976 the Commission refused summary judgment on Santo Domingo's claim that the Board's 1927 rejection of the 17,655-acre overlap with the La Majada and Mesita de Juana Lopez grants was a taking, because the record did not show which of two surveys of the grant was right (39 Ind. Cl. Comm. 241).
